title: Revit vs AutoCAD: Differences, Price & Which to Choose
excerpt: Revit builds a coordinated BIM model; AutoCAD is flexible drafting. Compare features, hardware, pricing and when the AEC Collection beats buying both.
body:
Revit and AutoCAD solve different problems. AutoCAD is a drafting tool: you draw lines, arcs and symbols that represent a building or a part. Revit is a BIM tool: you build a model out of real objects such as walls, doors, beams and ducts, and the plans, sections, schedules and quantities are generated from that model. If your deliverable is a coordinated building design, Revit is the long-term tool. If your deliverable is a drawing, AutoCAD (or AutoCAD LT) is usually enough.

## Drafting versus BIM

In AutoCAD, a wall in plan is two lines. A wall in section is another pair of lines, drawn separately. If the wall moves, you edit each view and hope you caught them all.

In Revit, the wall is one object with a type, a thickness, a height, a material and a position in the model. Every plan, section and elevation that shows it is a view onto the same model, so change the wall once and every drawing updates. Door and window schedules, area tables and material quantities come from the same data.

That is what BIM (building information modelling) means in practice: the model is the single source, and the drawings are outputs. It is why Revit is specified on public and large private projects, where coordination between architecture, structure and services needs to happen before construction rather than during it. Our category page on [BIM software](/bim-software) explains the wider concept.

## Side-by-side comparison

| | AutoCAD | Revit |
|---|---|---|
| Core approach | 2D drafting with 3D capability | Parametric 3D building model (BIM) |
| Main output | Drawings (DWG) | Model, drawings, schedules and quantities |
| Typical users | Draughtspeople, engineers, contractors, interior designers | Architects, structural and MEP designers, BIM coordinators |
| Change handling | Edit each drawing manually | Change once, views update |
| Multi-user working | Shared drawing files, xrefs | Worksharing for multi-user models |
| Open exchange | DWG | IFC import and export, plus links |
| Learning curve | Moderate | Steeper; needs templates and families |
| Platform | Windows, plus a Mac release with a different feature set | Windows only |
| Price per user per year, excl. GST | {{price:autocad}} | {{price:revit}} |
| Price per user per year, incl. 18% GST | {{gst:autocad}} | {{gst:revit}} |

See the product pages for [Autodesk Revit](/products/revit) and [AutoCAD](/products/autocad). Prices exclude GST unless stated, and a written quotation fixes the final price.

## What Revit gives you that AutoCAD does not

- **Coordination.** Architectural, structural and MEP elements live in one environment (or linked models), so clashes can be caught in the model. Revit works with Navisworks for clash coordination.
- **Automatic documentation.** Sheets, schedules and quantities update when the design changes. This removes a large category of errors from drawing sets.
- **Worksharing.** Several people can work on the same model, which a 2D drawing file does not support in the same way.
- **Families.** The family editor lets you build custom components such as furniture, fixtures and equipment, and reuse them across projects.
- **Open BIM exchange.** IFC import and export lets you share models with teams using other software.

## What AutoCAD gives you that Revit does not

AutoCAD wins on flexibility and speed for general drafting. It is a blank page: you can draw a site plan, a fabrication detail, an electrical single-line or a plant layout without first building a model. The subscription also includes the seven industry toolsets, which add discipline-specific objects for architecture, mechanical, electrical, MEP, mapping, plant design and raster clean-up. It carries web and mobile apps as well, handy on site.

AutoCAD is also far more universal as a file format and a skill. Contractors, suppliers and consultants across India exchange DWG files daily. Even firms that model in Revit usually keep AutoCAD for details, site drawings and for opening what everyone else sends.

## The cost of moving to Revit is not the licence

The Revit subscription costs more than AutoCAD, but the larger cost is adoption. A practice moving from 2D drafting needs templates, a family library, modelling standards and training before the benefit arrives. Expect productivity to dip for a few projects.

Hardware also changes. The catalogue lists 16 GB of RAM as a minimum for Revit and 32 GB or more for large models, a DirectX 11 capable GPU with 4 GB of VRAM, and SSD storage. Revit does not scale well across many cores, so strong single-thread performance matters more than a top-tier graphics card. It runs on Windows 11 and Windows 10 (64-bit) only, with no Mac release. Confirm current requirements on Autodesk's published page before you order workstations.

## A practical migration path

Few firms switch overnight. A path that tends to work looks like this:

1. **Pick one live project and a small team.** Two or three people who are keen and already strong in drafting. Avoid starting on a project with a punishing deadline.
2. **Build the basics first.** A project template with your standard levels, grids, sheet sizes, title blocks and annotation styles, plus a small family library of the doors, windows and fixtures you use repeatedly.
3. **Keep AutoCAD running in parallel.** Details, site drawings and consultant files will still arrive as DWG. Linking them into the model is normal.
4. **Agree modelling standards.** Who models what, how objects are named, and how much detail is needed at each stage. Without this, models become inconsistent and slow.
5. **Review hardware.** Large models punish under-specified machines, so check RAM and storage before the team scales up.
6. **Then widen.** Once the pilot has delivered a project, move more people across and decide whether the AEC Collection now makes sense.

## Common mistakes

**Buying Revit seats for everyone at once.** People without a modelling role still need to open drawings, and some can use lighter tools or Flex.

**Under-specifying workstations.** The licence is only part of the cost. A model that takes minutes to open will make the team resent the software.

**Expecting drawings to look like AutoCAD drawings immediately.** Revit output follows its own conventions. Allow time to tune line weights, annotation and sheet layouts to your drawing standards.

**Dropping AutoCAD too early.** Plenty of work still arrives as DWG, so a clean cut-over is rarely sensible in the first year.

## Lighter options: Revit LT and the LT suite

Not every firm needs the full product. [Autodesk Revit LT](/products/autodesk-revit-lt) is a simplified 3D BIM tool for producing 3D architectural designs and documentation. It is priced on enquiry, so ask for a quotation. Small architecture practices that want to move to BIM, without needing the full multi-discipline workflow, sometimes start here. Compare the feature list with what your projects actually require.

There is also [AutoCAD Revit LT Suite](/products/autocad-revit-lt-suite), which pairs Revit LT with AutoCAD LT for architectural design and documentation alongside 2D drafting. It is priced at {{price:autocad-revit-lt-suite}} per user per year, excluding GST. For a small firm that needs 3D BIM for design and 2D drafting for the rest, this can be easier than two separate subscriptions. If you only need 2D, see [AutoCAD vs AutoCAD LT](/blog/autocad-vs-autocad-lt).

## When the AEC Collection is the better answer

If a person needs both Revit and AutoCAD, price the collection before buying two subscriptions. The [AEC Collection](/products/aec-collection) bundles Revit, AutoCAD with its toolsets, Civil 3D, Navisworks Manage, Infraworks, 3ds Max, structural analysis tools and Autodesk Docs, and is priced at {{price:aec-collection}} per user per year excluding GST. Our guidance is consistent: with one product per user, standalone is cheaper; around two products it is close to break-even; with three or more, or with occasional need for specialised tools, the collection usually wins. We will compare it against your actual usage before quoting. See [the AEC Collection explained](/blog/autodesk-aec-collection-explained).

## Which should you choose?

**Choose AutoCAD if:**
- Your output is 2D drawings and details
- You work in many disciplines or trades and need a flexible drafting tool
- Your clients and partners exchange DWG files
- You are not ready to invest in BIM templates and training

**Choose Revit if:**
- You design buildings and need coordinated plans, sections, schedules and quantities
- Your projects require BIM deliverables or clash coordination
- Several disciplines work on one model
- You are prepared to invest in templates, families and training

**Choose both (or the AEC Collection) if:**
- Your team models in Revit but still produces AutoCAD details and site drawings
- You work with consultants who deliver in DWG

A common and sensible pattern is a mixed estate: Revit seats for the people who model, AutoCAD for those who detail and review, and Flex for occasional users. Read [Flex versus named-user subscriptions](/blog/autodesk-flex-versus-named-user-subscriptions) if that last group is large.

## Licensing and buying in India

Both products are licensed per named user. A subscription is assigned to one person, cannot be shared, but can be reassigned if someone leaves. Each named user can install on multiple machines and sign in on one at a time. See [Autodesk named-user licensing: what changed](/blog/autodesk-named-user-licensing-what-changed) for what this meant for practices used to shared licences.

Every order carries a GST invoice at 18%, generally claimable as input credit for registered businesses. For a mixed quotation, [send us an enquiry](/enquiry) with the number of people who model, draft and review. Monthly and multi-year terms can be quoted on request. More guidance is on our [Revit licensing page](/revit) and in the [CAD software guide](/cad-software).

faqs.question: Is Revit better than AutoCAD?
faqs.answer: Neither is better in general. Revit is stronger for coordinated building design because it generates drawings, schedules and quantities from one model. AutoCAD is stronger for flexible 2D drafting and details. Many firms use both, which is why the AEC Collection is worth pricing.

faqs.question: Can Revit replace AutoCAD completely?
faqs.answer: Rarely. Even firms that model in Revit usually keep AutoCAD for site drawings, details and for opening DWG files from consultants and suppliers. If you need both regularly, compare the AEC Collection against two separate subscriptions.

faqs.question: Does Revit run on a Mac?
faqs.answer: No. According to our product information Revit is Windows only, with no macOS release. It needs 64-bit Windows 11 or Windows 10, at least 16 GB RAM (more for large models) and an SSD. Check Autodesk's current requirements before ordering hardware.

faqs.question: What is Revit LT and how is it priced?
faqs.answer: Revit LT is a simplified 3D BIM tool for architectural design and documentation. It is priced on enquiry rather than listed, so please ask for a quotation. There is also an AutoCAD Revit LT Suite that combines Revit LT with AutoCAD LT.

faqs.question: Is it hard to move from AutoCAD to Revit?
faqs.answer: The software is learnable, but the real effort is in setting up templates, a family library and modelling standards. Expect a slower first project or two. Start with a pilot team and a real project instead of retraining everyone at once.

faqs.question: Should a small architecture firm in India buy Revit or the AEC Collection?
faqs.answer: If people use only Revit, the standalone subscription costs less. If they also need AutoCAD, Navisworks or Civil 3D, price the AEC Collection. We compare both against your actual usage before quoting, so send an enquiry with roles and project types.
